title: Model market-entry synchronization manifest: catalog, benchmarks, docs & comms
creator: Sofia Patel
description: This ticket is the coordination manifest for bringing a new model into the Redwood Model Catalog and executing the cross-team go-to-market sequence. It covers three pillars: 1) catalog metadata and model verification, 2) benchmark collection and performance guidance, and 3) documentation + release communications (release notes, blog, SDK samples). The goal is to provide a deterministic checklist, owners, and links to artifacts so launches are repeatable and auditable. Use this manifest to track readiness gates and collect final sign-offs from QA, Security, and Documentation leads.
checklist: Catalog entry: create catalog row with model_id, canonical name, size, canonical weights link, recommended variants and fallback mapping — owner: PM (Diego) — status: In Progress — GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/issues/512

Model verification: smoke-run inference with sample prompts (chat & completion), validate outputs for hallucinations and safety filters — owner: Eng (Jin Park) — status: Blocked (waiting GPU time) — internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/model-verification

Benchmark suite: run latency (p50/p95), throughput (tokens/s), memory, and cost-per-token on Hosted and Dedicated profiles — owner: SRE (Marcos) — status: Planned — benchmark dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/benchmarks/model-24817

Quantization guidance: recommend default quantization profile (Q4_0 or FP16) for Dedicated vs Private deployments and document trade-offs in cost/accuracy — owner: Research (Priya Rao) — status: In Progress

SDK examples and snippets: add new sample to SDK repo with streaming + function-calling example reflecting model capabilities — owner: DevX (Anita) — status: In Review — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1892

Docs: write Model Overview page (capabilities, known failure modes, prompt examples), add structured output schema examples, and include evaluation summary — owner: Docs (Liam O'Connor) — status: In Progress — Draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB2c3

Release notes: prepare single-line changelog entry + expanded notes with examples, breaking changes, and migration guidance (if any) — owner: PM (Diego) — status: Draft — PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/website/pull/745

Marketing assets: coordinate blog draft, launch deck, and social snippets; ensure screenshots reflect Console UI (catalog page) — owner: Growth (Nora Chen) — status: Planned — Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BxX
Legal & Compliance: confirm model license compatibility, export controls, and data handling constraints for Private deployments — owner: Legal (Arjun Singh) — status: In Progress
Security review: confirm KMS/HSM integration guidance (if model stores keys) and validate audit logging for Private install — owner: Security (Rita Gomez) — status: Not Started
Console rollout config: add model to Console model catalog, set default compute tiers, and configure rollout policy (canary -> 25% -> 100%) — owner: Console Eng (Theo) — status: Planned
Dedicated capacity profile: propose default GPU pool mapping and autoscaling knobs for expected QPS — owner: Infra (Katrin) — status: Planned
Customer comms & support playbook: create Support article with expected behaviors, known workarounds, and escalation path — owner: Support (Ethan) — status: Planned
Monitoring & quality alarms: define eval prompts, set regression detection thresholds, wire up dashboard alerts for prompt-sets tied to quality SLOs — owner: MLOps (Priya) — status: Planned
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Eng, Docs, Growth, Legal. Agreed cadence: tri-weekly sync until soft-launch. Action: Eng to prioritize smoke-run on dedicated dev pool.

2026-03-04: Decision to publish two recommended variants (fp16 and q4_0) in catalog with clear recommended use-cases. Trade-off discussion: q4_0 yields ~2.6x cost reduction but has subtle tokenization fidelity regressions on long-context summarization tasks. Research to capture example failure cases for docs.
2026-03-06: Docs PR template updated to include a 'Known weaknesses' section and structured example outputs. Docs lead requested a short canonical prompt set (10 prompts) for the evaluation summary.

2026-03-08: DevX PR for SDK sample created (PR #1892). QA noted streaming edge-case: mid-stream function calls may duplicate tokens for models using old-kv cache behavior. Eng assigned to patch runtime behavior or add client-side workaround.

2026-03-09: Benchmarks queued on Hosted staging fleet. Marcos requested a baseline run window (48h) to capture tail latency variability; SRE accepted but flagged potential cost overrun (estimate $1.2k). PM approved the budget for this run.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Latency vs Cost: enabling larger batch windows on Hosted improves throughput but risks increased p95 for interactive chat; agreed default is low-latency mode for chat routes and throughput mode opt-in for bulk generation.
Quality regressions with quantized variants: team will ship q4_0 as beta with clear catalog labeling and automatic fallback to fp16 on quality regression detection.
Private deployment constraints: some customers will not accept external benchmarking artifacts; Legal requested a summary template that can be redacted for on-prem attestations.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog row published with metadata, recommended variants, and fallback mapping.
Benchmark dashboard populated with p50/p95 latency, throughput, memory, and cost metrics for Hosted and Dedicated.
Documentation: Model Overview + Prompt Guide + Known Failures published in docs site.
Release notes merged to website PR and changelog entry present in release candidate.
Support playbook and escalation matrix added to internal Support wiki.
next_steps: Eng to complete smoke-run and post sample outputs to this ticket (due 2026-03-11).
Research to finalize quantization guidance and provide two representative fail-case prompts for docs (due 2026-03-12).
Docs to produce final Model Overview draft and link to SDK sample (due 2026-03-14).
Support and Legal to review playbook; finalize sign-offs before publish (target 2026-03-16).
notes: This manifest is intentionally prescriptive: every launch should map to this ticket or a child ticket. If we iteratively add more models, create PM-tied clones and reference this ticket as the canonical process. For API or semantic-breaking changes, include an explicit migration guide and customer notifications per the SLA communications playbook.
